caption: The drawing depicts a single, three-dimensional object that appears to be a fluted mold, possibly for baking or gelatin. The mold is centrally positioned on a plain, light beige background with no other objects present. The mold itself is rendered in a dark brown color, showing shading and gradation to give it a realistic and solid appearance. The mold has a cylindrical form with evenly spaced vertical flutes or ridges along its sides and a rounded, scalloped rim. There is a central cylindrical tube rising from its center, suggesting the mold is likely a bundt or ring mold. The artist's signature, "Richard Earne II," appears in the lower right corner of the drawing.
title: Cake Pan
cluster: #19 — Ceramic Arts: Pottery, Stoneware, and Porcelain
